```python
import bisect

class Solution:
    def maxValue(self, events: list[list[int]], k: int) -> int:
        events.sort(key=lambda x: x[1])
        n = len(events)
        ends = [e[1] for e in events]
        dp = [[0] * (k + 1) for _ in range(n + 1)]

        for i in range(1, n + 1):
            start, end, val = events[i - 1]
            p = bisect.bisect_left(ends, start)
            for j in range(1, k + 1):
                dp[i][j] = max(dp[i - 1][j], dp[p][j - 1] + val)

        return dp[n][k]
```

hints.title: Prefix Delta Formulation

hints.title: Replacing Single Element at Index i

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from collections import Counter

class Solution:
    def waysToPartition(self, nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
        n = len(nums)
        total = sum(nums)
        pref = [0] * n
        pref[0] = nums[0]
        for i in range(1, n):
            pref[i] = pref[i - 1] + nums[i]
        diffs = [2 * pref[i] - total for i in range(n - 1)]
        right_count = Counter(diffs)
        left_count = Counter()
        ans = right_count[0]
        for i in range(n):
            d = k - nums[i]
            curr = left_count[d] + right_count[-d]
            ans = max(ans, curr)
            if i < n - 1:
                diff = diffs[i]
                right_count[diff] -= 1
                left_count[diff] += 1
        return ans
```

```python
class Solution:
    def maxScore(self, cardPoints: list[int], k: int) -> int:
        n = len(cardPoints)
        window_size = n - k
        cur_sum = sum(cardPoints[:window_size])
        min_sum = cur_sum
        for i in range(window_size, n):
            cur_sum += cardPoints[i] - cardPoints[i - window_size]
            min_sum = min(min_sum, cur_sum)
        return sum(cardPoints) - min_sum
```

```python
class Solution:
    def maximumPopulation(self, logs: list[list[int]]) -> int:
        diff = [0] * 101
        for b, d in logs:
            diff[b - 1950] += 1
            diff[d - 1950] -= 1

        max_pop = 0
        best_year = 1950
        curr_pop = 0

        for i in range(101):

            if curr_pop > max_pop:
                max_pop = curr_pop
                best_year = 1950 + i

        return best_year
```

hints.title: Line of Waiting Customers
hints.text: At each rotation, new customers arrive and line up for the next gondola.

hints.title: Board at Most Four
hints.text: At most four waiting customers board each rotation, reducing queue size.

hints.title: Full Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def minOperationsMaxProfit(self, customers: list[int], boardingCost: int, runningCost: int) -> int:
        waiting = 0
        boarded = 0
        max_profit = 0
        best_rotations = -1
        rotations = 0
        i = 0
        while i < len(customers) or waiting > 0:
            if i < len(customers):
                waiting += customers[i]
                i += 1
            board = min(4, waiting)
            waiting -= board
            boarded += board
            rotations += 1
            profit = boarded * boardingCost - rotations * runningCost
            if profit > max_profit:
                max_profit = profit
                best_rotations = rotations
        return best_rotations
```

variables: n is number of arrival rounds

hints.title: Two Endpoints Choice
hints.text: At each operation step i, you either choose the leftmost available element or the rightmost available element.

hints.title: Derive Right Boundary from Left
hints.text: If left elements have been taken from the start, exactly i - left elements have been taken from the end, determining the right index.

hints.title: Two-Dimensional Dynamic Programming
hints.text: Define dp[i][left] as max score after i operations with left choices from front, taking the max of picking left or right.

hints.title: Full Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def maximumScore(self, nums: list[int], multipliers: list[int]) -> int:
        n = len(nums)
        m = len(multipliers)
        dp = [0] * (m + 1)

        for i in range(m - 1, -1, -1):
            mult = multipliers[i]
            for left in range(i + 1):
                right = n - 1 - (i - left)
                pick_left = mult * nums[left] + dp[left + 1]
                pick_right = mult * nums[right] + dp[left]
                dp[left] = max(pick_left, pick_right)

        return dp[0]
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Branching left and right at each of m steps explores 2^m possibilities.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Memoizing states (i, left) reduces computation to O(m^2) time and space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate deduces that right boundary is implicitly determined by n - 1 - (i - left).
complexity.notes: Optimal Big-O bounds.

hints.title: Start at Index K
hints.text: Initialize a window with left = k and right = k, with minimum element min_val = nums[k].

hints.title: Expand Toward Larger Neighbor
hints.text: At each expansion step, extend toward the side having the larger adjacent value to maintain highest possible min_val.

hints.title: Track Maximum Score
hints.text: Update min_val = min(min_val, new_element) and evaluate score = min_val * (right - left + 1) until entire array is covered.

hints.title: Full Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def maximumScore(self, nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
        n = len(nums)
        l, r = k, k
        min_val = nums[k]
        ans = min_val

        while l > 0 or r < n - 1:
            left_val = nums[l - 1] if l > 0 else -1
            right_val = nums[r + 1] if r < n - 1 else -1
            if left_val >= right_val:
                l -= 1
                min_val = min(min_val, nums[l])
            else:
                r += 1
                min_val = min(min_val, nums[r])
            ans = max(ans, min_val * (r - l + 1))

        return ans
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Evaluating all valid subarrays around k takes O(n^2) quadratic time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Greedy two-pointer window expansion covers all potential optimal boundaries in linear O(n) time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate proves that expanding toward the strictly larger neighboring element never misses the optimum.
complexity.notes: Optimal Big-O bounds.

class Solution:
```python
    def maxSumAfterOperation(self, nums: list[int]) -> int:
        dp0 = 0
        dp1 = 0
        ans = float('-inf')
```

```python
class Solution:
    def maxSumBST(self, root) -> int:
        self.max_sum = 0
        def dfs(node):
            if not node:
                return True, float("inf"), float("-inf"), 0
            l_valid, l_min, l_max, l_sum = dfs(node.left)
            r_valid, r_min, r_max, r_sum = dfs(node.right)
            if l_valid and r_valid and l_max < node.val < r_min:
                total = l_sum + r_sum + node.val
                self.max_sum = max(self.max_sum, total)
                return True, min(l_min, node.val), max(r_max, node.val), total
            return False, 0, 0, 0
        dfs(root)
        return self.max_sum
```

```python
class Solution:
    def maxSubarraySumCircular(self, nums: List[int]) -> int:
        total = 0
        cur_max, max_sum = 0, nums[0]
        cur_min, min_sum = 0, nums[0]
        for x in nums:
            cur_max = max(x, cur_max + x)
            max_sum = max(max_sum, cur_max)
            cur_min = min(x, cur_min + x)
            min_sum = min(min_sum, cur_min)
            total += x
        return max_sum if max_sum < 0 else max(max_sum, total - min_sum)
```

```python
class Solution:
    def maxSumRangeQuery(self, nums: list[int], requests: list[list[int]]) -> int:
        MOD = 10**9 + 7
        n = len(nums)
        diff = [0] * (n + 1)

            diff[r + 1] -= 1
        freq = [0] * n

            freq[i] = cur
        freq.sort()
        nums.sort()
        return sum(f * x for f, x in zip(freq, nums)) % MOD
```

```python
from typing import List

class Solution:
    def maxSumOfThreeSubarrays(self, nums: List[int], k: int) -> List[int]:
        n = len(nums)
        W = []
        curr = sum(nums[:k])
        W.append(curr)
        for i in range(k, n):
            curr += nums[i] - nums[i - k]
            W.append(curr)

        m = len(W)
        left = [0] * m
        best = 0
        for i in range(m):
            if W[i] > W[best]:
                best = i
            left[i] = best

        right = [0] * m
        best = m - 1
        for i in range(m - 1, -1, -1):
            if W[i] >= W[best]:
                best = i
            right[i] = best

        max_total = 0
        ans = []
        for mid in range(k, m - k):
            l, r = left[mid - k], right[mid + k]
            total = W[l] + W[mid] + W[r]
            if total > max_total:
                max_total = total
                ans = [l, mid, r]
        return ans
```

hints.text: Checking distinctness by building a set for every size-k window requires O(N * k) time. How can you maintain frequency counts and rolling sum simultaneously in constant time per step?

hints.title: Frequency Table Window Invariant

hints.text: Initialize window sum and frequency map for the first k elements. If map size is k, max_sum = window_sum, else 0. Slide right: add incoming element to sum and map; decrement count of outgoing element and remove if count reaches 0. If map size is k, update max_sum = max(max_sum, window_sum).

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def maximumSubarraySum(self, nums: List[int], k: int) -> int:
        from collections import defaultdict
        counts = defaultdict(int)
        curr_sum = 0
        max_sum = 0
        for i in range(k):
            counts[nums[i]] += 1
            curr_sum += nums[i]
        if len(counts) == k:
            max_sum = curr_sum
        for i in range(k, len(nums)):
            in_val, out_val = nums[i], nums[i - k]
            counts[in_val] += 1
            curr_sum += in_val
            counts[out_val] -= 1
            if counts[out_val] == 0:
                del counts[out_val]
            curr_sum -= out_val
            if len(counts) == k:
                max_sum = max(max_sum, curr_sum)
        return max_sum
```

```python
import heapq

class Solution:
    def minimumDeviation(self, nums: list[int]) -> int:
        pq = []
        min_val = float("inf")
        for x in nums:
            if x % 2 == 1:
                x *= 2
            pq.append(-x)
            min_val = min(min_val, x)
        heapq.heapify(pq)
        min_dev = float("inf")
        while True:
            max_val = -heapq.heappop(pq)
            min_dev = min(min_dev, max_val - min_val)
            if max_val % 2 == 1:
                break
            half = max_val // 2
            min_val = min(min_val, half)
            heapq.heappush(pq, -half)
        return min_dev
```

variables: max_val is maximum value in nums

complexity.notes: Optimal Big-O bounds.

```python
import math

class Solution:
    def minimizeError(self, prices: list[str], target: int) -> str:
        floors = []
        fracs = []
        for p in prices:
            val = float(p)
            f = math.floor(val)
            floors.append(f)
            frac = val - f
            if frac > 1e-9:
                fracs.append(frac)

        min_sum = sum(floors)
        max_sum = min_sum + len(fracs)
        if target < min_sum or target > max_sum:
            return "-1"

        k = target - min_sum
        fracs.sort(reverse=True)
        total_error = sum(1.0 - fracs[i] for i in range(k)) + sum(fracs[i] for i in range(k, len(fracs)))
        return f"{total_error:.3f}"
```

complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sorting fractional components enables an optimal greedy assignment in O(N log N) time.

```python
import bisect

class Solution:
    def minAbsoluteSumDiff(self, nums1: list[int], nums2: list[int]) -> int:
        MOD = 10**9 + 7
        n = len(nums1)
        sorted_nums1 = sorted(nums1)

        total = sum(abs(a - b) for a, b in zip(nums1, nums2))
        max_gain = 0

        for a, b in zip(nums1, nums2):
            orig_diff = abs(a - b)
            idx = bisect.bisect_left(sorted_nums1, b)
            if idx < n:
                max_gain = max(max_gain, orig_diff - abs(sorted_nums1[idx] - b))
            if idx > 0:
                max_gain = max(max_gain, orig_diff - abs(sorted_nums1[idx - 1] - b))

        return (total - max_gain) % MOD
```

```python
class Solution:
    def minMoves(self, nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
        p = [pos - i for i, pos in enumerate(i for i, x in enumerate(nums) if x == 1)]
        m = len(p)
        pref = [0] * (m + 1)
        for i in range(m):
            pref[i + 1] = pref[i] + p[i]
        ans = float('inf')
        radius = (k - 1) // 2
        for i in range(m - k + 1):
            mid = i + k // 2
            left_cost = p[mid] * (mid - i) - (pref[mid] - pref[i])
            right_cost = (pref[i + k] - pref[mid + 1]) - p[mid] * (i + k - 1 - mid)
            ans = min(ans, left_cost + right_cost)
        return ans
```

```python
import math
from collections import defaultdict

class Solution:
    def minAreaFreeRect(self, points: list[list[int]]) -> float:
        groups = defaultdict(list)
        n = len(points)
        for i in range(n):
            x1, y1 = points[i]
            for j in range(i + 1, n):
                x2, y2 = points[j]
                cx, cy = x1 + x2, y1 + y2
                d2 = (x1 - x2) ** 2 + (y1 - y2) ** 2
                groups[(cx, cy, d2)].append((x1, y1, x2, y2))
        min_area = float("inf")
        for pairs in groups.values():
            m = len(pairs)
            for i in range(m):
                x1, y1, x2, y2 = pairs[i]
                for j in range(i + 1, m):
                    x3, y3, _, _ = pairs[j]
                    side1 = math.hypot(x1 - x3, y1 - y3)
                    side2 = math.hypot(x2 - x3, y2 - y3)
                    min_area = min(min_area, side1 * side2)
        return min_area if min_area != float("inf") else 0.0
```

variables: K: number of pairs sharing identical midpoint and diagonal length

complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Grouping diagonal segments by center and length checks only valid rectangular configurations, running in sub-quadratic expected time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize geometric properties of rectangle diagonals: congruent and bisecting each other.
complexity.notes: Floating point coordinates should be represented with high precision or multiplied by 2 to keep integers.

class Solution:
```python
    def minCost(self, startPos: list[int], homePos: list[int], rowCosts: list[int], colCosts: list[int]) -> int:
        cost = 0
        r_step = 1 if homePos[0] >= startPos[0] else -1
        c_step = 1 if homePos[1] >= startPos[1] else -1

            cost += rowCosts[r]

            cost += colCosts[c]
```

```python
from typing import List
import heapq

class Solution:
    def mincostToHireWorkers(self, quality: List[int], wage: List[int], k: int) -> float:
        workers = sorted([(w / q, q) for w, q in zip(wage, quality)])
        max_heap = []
        sum_quality = 0
        min_cost = float('inf')

        for ratio, q in workers:
            heapq.heappush(max_heap, -q)
            sum_quality += q
            if len(max_heap) > k:
                sum_quality += heapq.heappop(max_heap)
            if len(max_heap) == k:
                min_cost = min(min_cost, ratio * sum_quality)

        return min_cost
```

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def minFallingPathSum(self, grid: list[list[int]]) -> int:
        n = len(grid)
        first_min, first_col = 0, -1
        second_min = 0
        for row in grid:
            cur_first_min, cur_first_col = float("inf"), -1
            cur_second_min = float("inf")
            for c in range(n):
                prev = second_min if c == first_col else first_min
                val = row[c] + prev
                if val < cur_first_min:
                    cur_second_min = cur_first_min
                    cur_first_min = val
                    cur_first_col = c
                elif val < cur_second_min:
                    cur_second_min = val
            first_min, first_col = cur_first_min, cur_first_col
            second_min = cur_second_min
        return first_min
```

```python
import heapq

class Solution:
    def minInterval(self, intervals: list[list[int]], queries: list[int]) -> list[int]:
        intervals.sort()
        sorted_queries = sorted([(q, i) for i, q in enumerate(queries)])

        pq = []
        ans = [-1] * len(queries)
        idx = 0
        n = len(intervals)

        for q, orig_idx in sorted_queries:
            while idx < n and intervals[idx][0] <= q:
                l, r = intervals[idx]
                heapq.heappush(pq, (r - l + 1, r))
                idx += 1

            while pq and pq[0][1] < q:
                heapq.heappop(pq)

            if pq:
                ans[orig_idx] = pq[0][0]

        return ans
```

complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Dual sorting and priority queue pruning evaluates active intervals in O((n + q) log n) time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate sorts queries and intervals, using a min-heap on interval length with lazy expiration.
complexity.notes: Optimal Big-O bounds.

```python
class Solution:
    def minMoves(self, nums: list[int], limit: int) -> int:
        n = len(nums)
        diff = [0] * (2 * limit + 2)
        for i in range(n // 2):
            a, b = nums[i], nums[n - 1 - i]
            if a > b:
                a, b = b, a
            # default 2 moves for all sums: diff[2] += 2
            diff[2] += 2
            # 1 move range: a + 1 to b + limit
            diff[a + 1] -= 1
            # 0 move point: a + b
            diff[a + b] -= 1
            diff[a + b + 1] += 1
            # 2 move range resumes: b + limit + 1
            diff[b + limit + 1] += 1
        curr = 0
        ans = n
        for s in range(2, 2 * limit + 1):
            curr += diff[s]
            ans = min(ans, curr)
        return ans
```

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def minNumberOfFrogs(self, croakOfFrogs: str) -> int:
        c = r = o = a = 0
        frogs = 0
        max_frogs = 0
        for ch in croakOfFrogs:
            if ch == "c":
                c += 1
                frogs += 1
                max_frogs = max(max_frogs, frogs)
            elif ch == "r":
                if c == 0: return -1
                c -= 1
                r += 1
            elif ch == "o":
                if r == 0: return -1
                r -= 1
                o += 1
            elif ch == "a":
                if o == 0: return -1
                o -= 1
                a += 1
            elif ch == "k":
                if a == 0: return -1
                a -= 1
                frogs -= 1
            else:
                return -1
        return max_frogs if frogs == 0 and c == r == o == a == 0 else -1
```

```python
class Solution:
    def minOperations(self, nums: list[int]) -> int:
        n = len(nums)
        unique = sorted(set(nums))
        ans = n
        r = 0
        for l in range(len(unique)):
            while r < len(unique) and unique[r] <= unique[l] + n - 1:
                r += 1
            count = r - l
            ans = min(ans, n - count)
        return ans
```

```python
class Solution:
    def minOperations(self, boxes: str) -> list[int]:
        n = len(boxes)
        ans = [0] * n

        ops = 0
        for i in range(n):
```

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
from typing import List
import heapq

class Solution:
    def minRefuelStops(self, target: int, startFuel: int, stations: List[List[int]]) -> int:
        max_heap = []
        stops = 0
        cur_fuel = startFuel
        prev_pos = 0
        stations.append([target, 0])

        for pos, fuel in stations:
            cur_fuel -= (pos - prev_pos)
            while max_heap and cur_fuel < 0:
                cur_fuel += -heapq.heappop(max_heap)
                stops += 1
            if cur_fuel < 0:
                return -1
            heapq.heappush(max_heap, -fuel)
            prev_pos = pos

        return stops
```

complexity.notes: Greedy fuel consumption with priority collection of passed stations.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Knapsack-style DP over state (station, stops) takes O(N^2) time and space.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Auxiliary priority collection requires O(N) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Deferred refuel choice: treat passed stations as fuel reserves to claim greedily when empty.

hints.title: Sliding Window Contraction Procedure

While current_sum is greater than or equal to target, record the candidate length right minus left plus one, subtract nums[left] from current_sum, and increment left. Return zero if min_len was never updated, else return min_len.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def minSubArrayLen(self, target: int, nums: list[int]) -> int:
        min_len = float('inf')
        left = 0
        current_sum = 0
        for right in range(len(nums)):
            current_sum += nums[right]
            while current_sum >= target:
                min_len = min(min_len, right - left + 1)
                current_sum -= nums[left]
                left += 1
        return 0 if min_len == float('inf') else min_len
```

```python
import bisect

class Solution:
    def minWastedSpace(self, packages: list[int], boxes: list[list[int]]) -> int:
        packages.sort()
        n = len(packages)
        pkg_sum = sum(packages)
        INF = float('inf')
        min_total_box = INF

        for supplier in boxes:
            supplier.sort()
            if supplier[-1] < packages[-1]:
                continue
            curr_box_sum = 0
            prev_idx = 0
            for b in supplier:
                idx = bisect.bisect_right(packages, b)
                count = idx - prev_idx
                curr_box_sum += count * b
                prev_idx = idx
                if idx == n:
                    break
            min_total_box = min(min_total_box, curr_box_sum)

        return (min_total_box - pkg_sum) % (10**9 + 7) if min_total_box != INF else -1
```

complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate checks supplier box[-1] >= packages[-1] and subtracts package sum.
complexity.notes: Optimal Big-O bounds.

```python
        ans = 0
```

hints.title: Complete Implementation

```python
import bisect

class Solution:
    def maximumBeauty(self, items: list[list[int]], queries: list[int]) -> list[int]:
        items.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])
        prices = [item[0] for item in items]
        max_beauty = []
        cur_max = 0
        for item in items:
            cur_max = max(cur_max, item[1])
            max_beauty.append(cur_max)

        res = []
        for q in queries:
            idx = bisect.bisect_right(prices, q) - 1
            res.append(max_beauty[idx] if idx >= 0 else 0)
        return res
```

complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sorting and prefix max precomputations reduce queries to independent binary searches.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should sort items by price and maintain monotonic running maximum beauty.

hints.text: Traverse post-order to compute each node sum. Increment frequency in counts map. After completing the tree visit, find the maximum count and return all keys matching that maximum.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
from collections import defaultdict
from typing import List, Optional

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right

class Solution:
    def findFrequentTreeSum(self, root: Optional[TreeNode]) -> List[int]:
        counts = defaultdict(int)

        def dfs(node: Optional[TreeNode]) -> int:
            if not node:
                return 0
            total = node.val + dfs(node.left) + dfs(node.right)
            counts[total] += 1
            return total

        dfs(root)
        max_freq = max(counts.values())
        return [s for s, c in counts.items() if c == max_freq]
```

variables: N: number of nodes in tree
complexity.notes: Post-order traversal visiting each node once with hash map tallying.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Recomputing sums repeatedly from top to bottom incurs quadratic O(N^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Bottom-up aggregation caches child subtree sums in recursion returns.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use post-order traversal to compute subtree sums in O(N) linear time.

```python
from typing import List

class Solution:
    def maxProfitAssignment(self, difficulty: List[int], profit: List[int], worker: List[int]) -> int:
        jobs = sorted(zip(difficulty, profit))
        worker.sort()
        ans = 0
        max_profit = 0
        i = 0
        n = len(jobs)

        for ability in worker:
            while i < n and jobs[i][0] <= ability:
                if jobs[i][1] > max_profit:
                    max_profit = jobs[i][1]
                i += 1
            ans += max_profit

        return ans
```

hints.title: Distinct Configurations Counting Obstacle

hints.title: Direct Count Backtracking Procedure
hints.text: Maintain boolean arrays or integer bitmasks for columns, main diagonals, and anti-diagonals. At row r == n, increment counter. For each column c from 0 to n - 1, if free, set flags, recurse on r + 1, and clear flags.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def totalNQueens(self, n: int) -> int:
        count = 0
        cols = [False] * n
        diag1 = [False] * (2 * n)
        diag2 = [False] * (2 * n)
        def backtrack(r: int):
            nonlocal count
            if r == n:
                count += 1
                return
            for c in range(n):
                if cols[c] or diag1[r - c + n] or diag2[r + c]:
                    continue
                cols[c] = diag1[r - c + n] = diag2[r + c] = True
                backtrack(r + 1)
                cols[c] = diag1[r - c + n] = diag2[r + c] = False
        backtrack(0)
        return count
```

variables: N: board dimension and queen count (1 <= N <= 9)
complexity.notes: Direct backtracking without board string allocations running in O(N!) time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all combinations of coordinates takes O(N^(2N)) steps.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Boolean flags occupy O(N) space, avoiding 2D board allocations.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Using constant-time diagonal index mapping r - c + n.

hints.title: Non-Attacking Placement Obstacle

hints.title: Diagonal Invariant Formulation

hints.title: Row-by-Row Placement Procedure
hints.text: Recurse row by row from 0 to n. For row r, iterate column c from 0 to n - 1. If c is in occupied columns, (r - c) in occupied diagonals, or (r + c) in occupied anti-diagonals, skip. Otherwise record state, place queen, recurse on r + 1, and backtrack by clearing sets.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def solveNQueens(self, n: int) -> List[List[str]]:
        res = []
        cols = set()
        diag1 = set()   # r - c
        diag2 = set()   # r + c
        board = [['.' for _ in range(n)] for _ in range(n)]
        def backtrack(r: int):
            if r == n:
                res.append([''.join(row) for row in board])
                return
            for c in range(n):
                if c in cols or (r - c) in diag1 or (r + c) in diag2:
                    continue
                cols.add(c)
                diag1.add(r - c)
                diag2.add(r + c)
                board[r][c] = 'Q'
                backtrack(r + 1)
                board[r][c] = '.'
                cols.remove(c)
                diag1.remove(r - c)
                diag2.remove(r + c)
        backtrack(0)
        return res
```

variables: N: board dimension and queen count (1 <= N <= 9)
complexity.notes: First queen has N choices, second has at most N-2 choices, bounding complexity by O(N!).
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing all (N^2 choose N) board arrangements exceeds feasible computation.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Constant-time diagonal state lookups require O(N) auxiliary set memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Using row-by-row placement to inherently satisfy the row constraint.

hints.title: Digit Permutation Next Greater Step
hints.text: The problem is equivalent to finding the next lexicographical permutation of the decimal digits of integer n.

hints.title: Pivot Scan and Suffix Reversal
hints.text: Scan right-to-left for the first decreasing digit. Swap it with the smallest larger digit to its right, then reverse the descending suffix.

hints.text: Convert the mutated digit list back to an integer. If no next permutation exists or if the resulting integer exceeds 2^31 - 1, return minus 1.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def nextGreaterElement(self, n: int) -> int:
        digits = list(str(n))
        i = len(digits) - 2
        while i >= 0 and digits[i] >= digits[i + 1]:
            i -= 1
        if i < 0:
            return -1
        j = len(digits) - 1
        while digits[j] <= digits[i]:
            j -= 1
        digits[i], digits[j] = digits[j], digits[i]
        digits[i + 1:] = reversed(digits[i + 1:])
        val = int("".join(digits))
        return val if val <= 2**31 - 1 else -1
```

variables: N: value of n (at most 10 decimal digits)
complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(log N) time and O(log N) auxiliary space.

```python
class Solution:
    def findNthDigit(self, n: int) -> int:
        length = 1
        count = 9
        start = 1
        while n > length * count:
            n -= length * count
            length += 1
            count *= 10
            start *= 10
        start += (n - 1) // length
        return int(str(start)[(n - 1) % length])
```

```python
class Solution:
    def numMusicPlaylists(self, n: int, goal: int, k: int) -> int:
        MOD = 1_000_000_007
        dp = [0] * (n + 1)
        dp[0] = 1
        for i in range(1, goal + 1):
            nxt = [0] * (n + 1)
            for j in range(1, min(i, n) + 1):
                new_song = dp[j - 1] * (n - j + 1)
                old_song = dp[j] * max(0, j - k)
                nxt[j] = (new_song + old_song) % MOD
            dp = nxt
        return dp[n]
```

```python
class Solution:
    def countSubTrees(self, n: int, edges: list[list[int]], labels: str) -> list[int]:
        import sys
        sys.setrecursionlimit(200000)
        graph = [[] for _ in range(n)]
        for u, v in edges:
            graph[u].append(v)
            graph[v].append(u)
        ans = [0] * n
        def dfs(u, parent):
            counts = [0] * 26
            u_label = ord(labels[u]) - ord("a")
            counts[u_label] = 1
            for v in graph[u]:
                if v != parent:
                    child_counts = dfs(v, u)
                    for i in range(26):
                        counts[i] += child_counts[i]
            ans[u] = counts[u_label]
            return counts
        dfs(0, -1)
        return ans
```

```python
import math
from collections import defaultdict

class Solution:
    def interchangeableRectangles(self, rectangles: list[list[int]]) -> int:
        freq = defaultdict(int)
        for w, h in rectangles:
            g = math.gcd(w, h)
            freq[(w // g, h // g)] += 1
        ans = 0
        for cnt in freq.values():
            ans += cnt * (cnt - 1) // 2
        return ans
```

hints.text: If a strictly shorter path is found, update distance and inherit ways[u]. If an equal distance is found, add ways[u] modulo 1,000,000,007.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import heapq

class Solution:
    def countPaths(self, n: int, roads: list[list[int]]) -> int:
        MOD = 1_000_000_007
        adj = [[] for _ in range(n)]
        for u, v, time in roads:
            adj[u].append((v, time))
            adj[v].append((u, time))
            
        dist = [float("inf")] * n
        ways = [0] * n
        dist[0] = 0
        ways[0] = 1
        
        pq = [(0, 0)]
        while pq:
            d, u = heapq.heappop(pq)
            if d > dist[u]:
                continue
            for v, time in adj[u]:
                nd = d + time
                if nd < dist[v]:
                    dist[v] = nd
                    ways[v] = ways[u]
                    heapq.heappush(pq, (nd, v))
                elif nd == dist[v]:
                    ways[v] = (ways[v] + ways[u]) % MOD
                    
        return ways[n - 1]
```

complexity.notes: Modified Dijkstra tracking path frequencies alongside minimal travel duration.

complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Priority heap processes each edge at most once per optimal arrival.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize tracking path counts during Dijkstra relaxation.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import math

class Solution:
    def numOfWays(self, nums: list[int]) -> int:
        MOD = 10**9 + 7
        def count_ways(arr):
            if len(arr) <= 2:
                return 1
            root = arr[0]
            left = [x for x in arr[1:] if x < root]
            right = [x for x in arr[1:] if x > root]
            ways = math.comb(len(left) + len(right), len(left)) % MOD
            return (ways * count_ways(left) * count_ways(right)) % MOD
        return (count_ways(nums) - 1) % MOD
```

hints.text: maintain running prefix parity mask where the i-th bit flips whenever character (a + i) is encountered.

hints.title: Querying 0 or 1 Bit Flips

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def wonderfulSubstrings(self, word: str) -> int:
        counts = [0] * 1024
        counts[0] = 1
        mask = 0
        res = 0
        for ch in word:
            mask ^= 1 << (ord(ch) - ord('a'))
            res += counts[mask]
            for b in range(10):
                res += counts[mask ^ (1 << b)]
            counts[mask] += 1
        return res
```

complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Prefix parity bitmask runs in O(10 * N) = O(N) linear time using a fixed 1024-element frequency array.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should map character parities to bitmasks and evaluate 11 mask variations (0 flips + 10 single-bit flips).

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
from typing import List

class Solution:
    def atMostNGivenDigitSet(self, digits: List[str], n: int) -> int:
        s = str(n)
        k = len(s)
        m = len(digits)
        ans = sum(m ** i for i in range(1, k))

        for i, ch in enumerate(s):
            smaller = sum(d < ch for d in digits)
            ans += smaller * (m ** (k - 1 - i))
            if ch not in digits:
                return ans
        return ans + 1
```

hints.title: Index-Parity Node Reordering Obstacle
hints.text: Splitting by node values rather than node indices produces incorrect arrangements. How can interleaving two reference chains allow you to regroup odd and even indexed nodes in a single pass?

hints.title: Odd and Even Splicing Invariant
hints.text: Maintain separate odd and even pointers, alternating link advances while preserving the even chain head to attach at the end of the odd chain.

hints.title: Dual-Chain Interleaving Procedure
hints.text: If head is null, return head. Set odd to head and even to head.next, saving evenHead as even. While even and even.next exist: set odd.next to even.next, advance odd, set even.next to odd.next, and advance even. Finally, link odd.next to evenHead. Return head.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def oddEvenList(self, head: Optional[ListNode]) -> Optional[ListNode]:
        if not head or not head.next:
            return head
        odd = head
        even = head.next
        even_head = even
        while even and even.next:
            odd.next = even.next
            odd = odd.next
            even.next = odd.next
            even = even.next
        odd.next = even_head
        return head
```

variables: N: number of nodes in list (0 <= N <= 10^4)
complexity.notes: Single pass grouping odd and even indices in O(1) space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Allocating two new node arrays violates the constant extra space requirement.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Direct in-place pointer leapfrogging runs in linear time with zero extra heap allocations.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Preserving the original relative order among odd nodes and among even nodes.

```python
class Solution:
    def numPairsDivisibleBy60(self, time: list[int]) -> int:
        count = [0] * 60
        res = 0
        for t in time:
            r = t % 60
            res += count[(60 - r) % 60]
            count[r] += 1
        return res
```

hints.title: Linear Auxiliary Allocation Obstacle
hints.text: Copying all node values to an array consumes linear auxiliary space. How can finding the midpoint and inverting the latter half allow symmetric comparison in O(1) space?

hints.text: Locate the list midpoint, reverse the second half in-place, and compare corresponding nodes from both ends inward.

hints.title: Midpoint Split and Inward Check Procedure

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def isPalindrome(self, head: Optional[ListNode]) -> bool:
        if not head or not head.next:
            return True
        slow = head
        fast = head
        while fast and fast.next:
            slow = slow.next
            fast = fast.next.next
        prev = None
        curr = slow
        while curr:
            nxt = curr.next
            curr.next = prev
            prev = curr
            curr = nxt
        p1 = head
        p2 = prev
        while p2:
            if p1.val != p2.val:
                return False
            p1 = p1.next
            p2 = p2.next
        return True
```

variables: N: number of nodes in list (1 <= N <= 10^5)
complexity.notes: Find midpoint, reverse second half in-place, and compare in O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Buffering node values in a dynamic array requires O(N) extra memory, failing the O(1) follow-up challenge.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: In-place half-reversal achieves O(1) auxiliary space with only two linear passes.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Ability to find the midpoint with fast/slow pointers and reverse a sublist cleanly.

```python
class Solution:
    def minCut(self, s: str) -> int:
        n = len(s)
        dp = list(range(n))

        for mid in range(n):
            l, r = mid, mid
            while l >= 0 and r < n and s[l] == s[r]:
                dp[r] = 0 if l == 0 else min(dp[r], dp[l - 1] + 1)
                l -= 1
                r += 1
            l, r = mid, mid + 1
            while l >= 0 and r < n and s[l] == s[r]:
                dp[r] = 0 if l == 0 else min(dp[r], dp[l - 1] + 1)
                l -= 1
                r += 1

        return dp[-1]
```

```python
class Solution:
    def canPermutePalindrome(self, s: str) -> bool:
        from collections import Counter
        counts = Counter(s)
        odd_count = sum(1 for c in counts.values() if c % 2 == 1)
        return odd_count <= 1
```

```python
class Solution:
    def countSubstrings(self, s: str) -> int:
        n = len(s)
        count = 0
        for center in range(2 * n - 1):
            l = center // 2
            r = l + (center % 2)
            while l >= 0 and r < n and s[l] == s[r]:
                count += 1
                l -= 1
                r += 1
        return count
```

```python
import bisect

class Solution:
    def minimumDifference(self, nums: list[int]) -> int:
        n = len(nums) // 2
        total = sum(nums)
        target = total // 2
        left_sums = [[] for _ in range(n + 1)]
        right_sums = [[] for _ in range(n + 1)]

        for mask in range(1 << n):
            sz = bin(mask).count('1')
            s_l = sum(nums[i] for i in range(n) if (mask >> i) & 1)
            left_sums[sz].append(s_l)
            s_r = sum(nums[n + i] for i in range(n) if (mask >> i) & 1)
            right_sums[sz].append(s_r)

        for sz in range(n + 1):
            right_sums[sz].sort()

        ans = float('inf')
        for k in range(n + 1):
            req = n - k
            r_list = right_sums[req]
            for sl in left_sums[k]:
                ideal = target - sl
                idx = bisect.bisect_left(r_list, ideal)
                if idx < len(r_list):
                    s1 = sl + r_list[idx]
                    s2 = total - s1
                    ans = min(ans, abs(s1 - s2))
                if idx > 0:
                    s1 = sl + r_list[idx - 1]
                    s2 = total - s1
                    ans = min(ans, abs(s1 - s2))
        return ans
```

complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sorting subset sums per element count enables logarithmic lookups.

```python
class Solution:
    def partition(self, head: Optional[ListNode], x: int) -> Optional[ListNode]:
        small_dummy = ListNode(0)
        large_dummy = ListNode(0)
        small = small_dummy
        large = large_dummy
        curr = head
        while curr:
            if curr.val < x:
                small.next = curr
                small = small.next
            else:
                large.next = curr
                large = large.next
            curr = curr.next
        large.next = None
        small.next = large_dummy.next
        return small_dummy.next
```

complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Using two dummy heads constructs stable partitions in O(1) auxiliary space without list reallocation.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Ensuring large.next is explicitly terminated with null to prevent circular link references.

class Solution:
```python
    def pathInZigZagTree(self, label: int) -> list[int]:
        res = []
        curr = label
        while curr >= 1:
            res.append(curr)
            depth = curr.bit_length()

            max_val = (1 << depth) - 1
```

```python
from collections import defaultdict
from typing import Optional

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right

class Solution:
    def pathSum(self, root: Optional[TreeNode], targetSum: int) -> int:
        prefix_counts = defaultdict(int)
        prefix_counts[0] = 1
        count = 0

        def dfs(node: Optional[TreeNode], curr_sum: int):
            nonlocal count
            if not node:
                return
            curr_sum += node.val
            count += prefix_counts[curr_sum - targetSum]
            prefix_counts[curr_sum] += 1
            dfs(node.left, curr_sum)
            dfs(node.right, curr_sum)
            prefix_counts[curr_sum] -= 1

        dfs(root, 0)
        return count
```

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def getPermutation(self, n: int, k: int) -> str:
        nums = [str(i) for i in range(1, n + 1)]
        fact = 1
        for i in range(1, n):
            fact *= i
        k -= 1
        res = []
        for i in range(n - 1, 0, -1):
            idx = k // fact
            res.append(nums.pop(idx))
            k %= fact
            fact //= i
        res.append(nums[0])
        return "".join(res)
```

hints.text:
```python
import math

class Solution:
    def getProbability(self, balls: list[int]) -> float:
        k = len(balls)
        n = sum(balls) // 2
        memo = {}
        def dfs(i, count1, d1, d2):
            if count1 > n:
                return 0, 0
            if i == k:
                if count1 == n:
                    return (1 if d1 == d2 else 0), 1
                return 0, 0
            state = (i, count1, d1, d2)
            if state in memo:
                return memo[state]
            valid_ways, total_ways = 0, 0
            b = balls[i]
            for c in range(b + 1):
                ways = math.comb(b, c)
                nd1 = d1 + (1 if c > 0 else 0)
                nd2 = d2 + (1 if b - c > 0 else 0)
                v, t = dfs(i + 1, count1 + c, nd1, nd2)
                valid_ways += v * ways
                total_ways += t * ways
            memo[state] = (valid_ways, total_ways)
            return valid_ways, total_ways
        valid, total = dfs(0, 0, 0, 0)
        return valid / total
```

variables: N: half the total number of balls
complexity.notes: Memoized state captures (color index, count of balls in box 1, distinct colors in box 1, distinct colors in box 2).

complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Color-wise distribution with combination weights groups identical ball permutations together.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: DFS with multinomial coefficient counting and memoization across distinct color states.

hints.text: If no servers are available at task arrival time, advance the clock directly to the earliest completion time.

hints.title: Full Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import heapq

class Solution:
    def assignTasks(self, servers: list[int], tasks: list[int]) -> list[int]:
        free = [(w, i) for i, w in enumerate(servers)]
        heapq.heapify(free)
        busy = []

        ans = []
        curr_time = 0

        for i, task_dur in enumerate(tasks):
            curr_time = max(curr_time, i)
            if not free and busy[0][0] > curr_time:
                curr_time = busy[0][0]

            while busy and busy[0][0] <= curr_time:
                _, w, s_idx = heapq.heappop(busy)
                heapq.heappush(free, (w, s_idx))

            w, s_idx = heapq.heappop(free)
            ans.append(s_idx)
            heapq.heappush(busy, (curr_time + task_dur, w, s_idx))

        return ans
```

complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Dual priority queues process all events in O((m + n) log n) time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate handles clock fast-forwarding when all servers are currently occupied.
complexity.notes: Optimal Big-O bounds.

hints.title: Two-Pass Forward and Backward In-Place Scan

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def productExceptSelf(self, nums: list[int]) -> list[int]:
        n = len(nums)
        res = [1] * n
        prefix = 1
        for i in range(n):
            res[i] = prefix
            prefix *= nums[i]
        suffix = 1
        for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
            res[i] *= suffix
            suffix *= nums[i]
        return res
```

complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Building prefix products directly inside the output array and using a single scalar for suffix products reduces auxiliary space from O(N) to O(1) while maintaining O(N) linear time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Respecting the no-division constraint, handling multiple zeros correctly, achieving O(1) extra space beyond the result array, and writing clean two-pass logic.

```python
    def numRabbits(self, answers: List[int]) -> int:
```

```python
import random

class Solution:
    def __init__(self, m: int, n: int):
        self.m = m
        self.n = n
        self.total = m * n
        self.mapping = {}

    def flip(self) -> list[int]:
        r = random.randint(0, self.total - 1)
        self.total -= 1
        actual = self.mapping.get(r, r)
        self.mapping[r] = self.mapping.get(self.total, self.total)
        return [actual // self.n, actual % self.n]

    def reset(self) -> None:
        self.mapping.clear()
        self.total = self.m * self.n
```

hints.title: Two-Stage Sampling Blueprint

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import bisect
import random

class Solution:
    def __init__(self, rects: list[list[int]]):
        self.rects = rects
        self.prefix = []
        total = 0
        for x1, y1, x2, y2 in rects:
            points = (x2 - x1 + 1) * (y2 - y1 + 1)
            total += points
            self.prefix.append(total)
        self.total = total

    def pick(self) -> list[int]:
        target = random.randint(1, self.total)
        idx = bisect.bisect_left(self.prefix, target)
        x1, y1, x2, y2 = self.rects[idx]
        return [random.randint(x1, x2), random.randint(y1, y2)]
```

complexity.notes: Initial construction builds prefix array in O(N); each pick runs in O(log N) binary search time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Picking rectangles uniformly creates bias toward points in smaller rectangles.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Prefix sum array enables logarithmic binary search rectangle selection.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Correct point count formula including both endpoints: (x2 - x1 + 1) * (y2 - y1 + 1).

```python
class Solution:
    def getModifiedArray(self, length: int, updates: List[List[int]]) -> List[int]:
        arr = [0] * (length + 1)
        for s, e, inc in updates:
            arr[s] += inc
            arr[e + 1] -= inc
        res = [0] * length
        running = 0
        for i in range(length):
            running += arr[i]
            res[i] = running
        return res
```

```python
class Solution:

        target = abs(target)
        k = 0
        total = 0
```

```python
class Solution:
    def reorderSpaces(self, text: str) -> str:
        total_spaces = text.count(" ")
        words = text.split()
        n = len(words)
        if n == 1:
            return words[0] + " " * total_spaces
        gap = total_spaces // (n - 1)
        rem = total_spaces % (n - 1)
        return (" " * gap).join(words) + " " * rem
```

```python
class Solution:
    def rearrangeString(self, s: str, k: int) -> str:
        if k <= 1:
            return s
        from collections import Counter, deque
        import heapq
        counts = Counter(s)
        max_heap = [(-cnt, ch) for ch, cnt in counts.items()]
        heapq.heapify(max_heap)
        cooldown = deque()
        res = []
        while max_heap:
            cnt, ch = heapq.heappop(max_heap)
            res.append(ch)
            cooldown.append((cnt + 1, ch))
            if len(cooldown) >= k:
                ready_cnt, ready_ch = cooldown.popleft()
                if ready_cnt < 0:
                    heapq.heappush(max_heap, (ready_cnt, ready_ch))
        return "".join(res) if len(res) == len(s) else ""
```

complexity.notes: Optimal greedy solution running in O(N log A) time and O(A) auxiliary space bounded by alphabet size.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Arbitrary placement quickly creates unavoidable adjacent traps with leftover frequent letters.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Max-heap prioritizes urgent characters while cooldown queue enforces minimum k separation.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should handle edge cases k = 0 or k = 1 and detect impossible configurations when result length < s length.

```python
from collections import defaultdict
from typing import List

class Solution:
    def findItinerary(self, tickets: List[List[str]]) -> List[str]:
        adj = defaultdict(list)
        for u, v in sorted(tickets, reverse=True):
            adj[u].append(v)

        route = []
        def dfs(airport: str):
            while adj[airport]:
                nxt = adj[airport].pop()
                dfs(nxt)
            route.append(airport)

        dfs("JFK")
        return route[::-1]
```

```python
from typing import List

class Solution:
    def rectangleArea(self, rectangles: List[List[int]]) -> int:
        MOD = 1_000_000_007
        xs = sorted(list(set([r[0] for r in rectangles] + [r[2] for r in rectangles])))
        total_area = 0

        for i in range(len(xs) - 1):
            x1, x2 = xs[i], xs[i + 1]
            width = x2 - x1
            intervals = []
            for rx1, ry1, rx2, ry2 in rectangles:
                if rx1 <= x1 and rx2 >= x2:
                    intervals.append((ry1, ry2))
            intervals.sort()
            covered_y = 0
            cur_bottom = -1
            for y1, y2 in intervals:
                cur_bottom = max(cur_bottom, y1)
                if y2 > cur_bottom:
                    covered_y += y2 - cur_bottom
                    cur_bottom = y2
            total_area = (total_area + covered_y * width) % MOD

        return total_area
```

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
from collections import Counter

class Solution:
    def minSetSize(self, arr: list[int]) -> int:
        counts = Counter(arr)
        freqs = sorted(counts.values(), reverse=True)
        removed = 0
        needed = (len(arr) + 1) // 2
        ans = 0
        for f in freqs:
            removed += f
            ans += 1
            if removed >= needed:
                break
        return ans
```

class Solution:
```python
    def removeZeroSumSublists(self, head: Optional[ListNode]) -> Optional[ListNode]:
        dummy = ListNode(0, head)
        prefix = 0
        seen = {}

            curr = curr.next
```

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def minimumDeletions(self, nums: list[int]) -> int:
        n = len(nums)
        if n <= 2:
            return n

        min_idx = nums.index(min(nums))
        max_idx = nums.index(max(nums))

        i = min(min_idx, max_idx)
        j = max(min_idx, max_idx)

        both_front = j + 1
        both_back = n - i
        one_each = (i + 1) + (n - j)

        return min(both_front, both_back, one_each)
```

```python
class Solution:
    def reorderList(self, head: Optional[ListNode]) -> None:
        if not head or not head.next:
            return
        slow, fast = head, head
        while fast and fast.next:
            slow = slow.next
            fast = fast.next.next
        prev, curr = None, slow.next
        slow.next = None
        while curr:
            nxt = curr.next
            curr.next = prev
            prev = curr
            curr = nxt
        first, second = head, prev
        while second:
            tmp1, tmp2 = first.next, second.next
            first.next = second
            second.next = tmp1
            first, second = tmp1, tmp2
```

```python
from collections import Counter

class Solution:
    def balancedString(self, s: str) -> int:
        count = Counter(s)
        n = len(s)
        k = n // 4
        if all(count[c] <= k for c in 'QWER'):
            return 0
            
        ans = n
        left = 0
        for right in range(n):
            count[s[right]] -= 1
            while all(count[c] <= k for c in 'QWER'):
                ans = min(ans, right - left + 1)
                count[s[left]] += 1
                left += 1
        return ans
```

class Solution:
```python
    def restoreArray(self, adjacentPairs: list[list[int]]) -> list[int]:
        adj = defaultdict(list)
        for u, v in adjacentPairs:
            adj[u].append(v)
            adj[v].append(u)
```

hints.title: Complete Implementation

```python
class Solution:
    def reverse(self, x: int) -> int:
        sign = -1 if x < 0 else 1
        x = abs(x)
        rev = 0
        limit = (1 << 31) - 1
        while x > 0:
            digit = x % 10
            x //= 10
            if rev > (limit - digit) // 10:
                return 0
            rev = rev * 10 + digit
        ans = sign * rev
        return ans if -(1 << 31) <= ans <= limit else 0
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Converting to string and parsing may still overflow 32-bit signed integer types in statically typed languages like C++ or Java.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Iterative decimal digit extraction completes in at most 10 iterations with O(1) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should handle the sign, prevent 32-bit integer overflow, and return 0 on overflow.

```python
class Solution:
    def reverseBetween(self, head: Optional[ListNode], left: int, right: int) -> Optional[ListNode]:
        if not head or left == right:
            return head
        dummy = ListNode(0, head)
        prev = dummy
        for _ in range(left - 1):
            prev = prev.next
        curr = prev.next
        for _ in range(right - left):
            nxt = curr.next
            curr.next = nxt.next
            nxt.next = prev.next
            prev.next = nxt
        return dummy.next
```

```python
class Solution:
    def reverseEvenLengthGroups(self, head: Optional[ListNode]) -> Optional[ListNode]:
        prev_group_tail = None
        curr = head
        group_len = 1

        while curr:
            count = 0
            temp = curr
            while temp and count < group_len:
                count += 1
                temp = temp.next

            if count % 2 == 0:
                rev_prev = None
                rev_curr = curr
                for _ in range(count):
                    nxt = rev_curr.next
                    rev_curr.next = rev_prev
                    rev_prev = rev_curr
                    rev_curr = nxt

                if prev_group_tail:
                    prev_group_tail.next = rev_prev
                curr.next = rev_curr
                prev_group_tail = curr
                curr = rev_curr
            else:
                for _ in range(count):
                    prev_group_tail = curr
                    curr = curr.next

            group_len += 1

        return head
```

```python
class Solution:
    def reverseKGroup(self, head: Optional[ListNode], k: int) -> Optional[ListNode]:
        dummy = ListNode(0, head)
        group_prev = dummy
        while True:
            kth = group_prev
            for _ in range(k):
                kth = kth.next
                if not kth:
                    return dummy.next
            group_next = kth.next
            prev, curr = kth.next, group_prev.next
            while curr != group_next:
                nxt = curr.next
                curr.next = prev
                prev = curr
                curr = nxt
            tail = group_prev.next
            group_prev.next = kth
            group_prev = tail
```

```python
class Solution:
    def maxValueAfterReverse(self, nums: list[int]) -> int:
        base = sum(abs(nums[i] - nums[i + 1]) for i in range(len(nums) - 1))
        n = len(nums)
        res = base

        for i in range(n - 1):
            res = max(res, base - abs(nums[i] - nums[i + 1]) + abs(nums[0] - nums[i + 1]))
            res = max(res, base - abs(nums[i] - nums[i + 1]) + abs(nums[-1] - nums[i]))

        min_hi = float("inf")
        max_lo = float("-inf")
        for i in range(n - 1):
            a, b = nums[i], nums[i + 1]
            min_hi = min(min_hi, max(a, b))
            max_lo = max(max_lo, min(a, b))

        return max(res, base + max(0, (max_lo - min_hi) * 2))
```

```python
class Solution:
    def cleanRoom(self, robot):
        directions = [(-1, 0), (0, 1), (1, 0), (0, -1)]
        visited = set()

        def go_back():
            robot.turnRight()
            robot.turnRight()
            robot.move()
            robot.turnRight()
            robot.turnRight()

        def dfs(r, c, d):
            visited.add((r, c))
            robot.clean()
            for i in range(4):
                nd = (d + i) % 4
                nr = r + directions[nd][0]
                nc = c + directions[nd][1]
                if (nr, nc) not in visited and robot.move():
                    dfs(nr, nc, nd)
                    go_back()
                robot.turnRight()

        dfs(0, 0, 0)
```

complexity.notes: Visits every reachable cell and backtracks once, making four turns at each location.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Random walks or uncoordinated exploration loops infinitely or leaves dead-ends unvisited.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Visited relative coordinate set avoids redundant exploration without room dimension foreknowledge.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Correct go_back physical retreat sequence that precisely restores robot orientation.

```python
class Solution:
    def rotate(self, nums: List[int], k: int) -> None:
        n = len(nums)
        k %= n
        def reverse(l: int, r: int):
            while l < r:
                nums[l], nums[r] = nums[r], nums[l]
                l += 1
                r -= 1
        reverse(0, n - 1)
        reverse(0, k - 1)
        reverse(k, n - 1)
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Rotating one step at a time takes O(N * K) quadratic time, while allocating a second array consumes O(N) auxiliary space.

```python
class Solution:
    def maxRotateFunction(self, nums: List[int]) -> int:
        n = len(nums)
        total_sum = sum(nums)
        cur_f = sum(i * x for i, x in enumerate(nums))
        max_f = cur_f
        for k in range(1, n):
            cur_f = cur_f + total_sum - n * nums[n - k]
            max_f = max(max_f, cur_f)
        return max_f
```

hints.text: Check if head is null or head.next is null or k is 0. Traverse to compute total length and stop at tail. Link tail.next to head. Compute effective shift steps = length - (k % length). Advance tail by effective steps, save newHead as tail.next, and set tail.next to null.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

```python
class Solution:
    def rotateRight(self, head: Optional[ListNode], k: int) -> Optional[ListNode]:
        if not head or not head.next or k == 0:
            return head
        length = 1
        tail = head
        while tail.next:
            tail = tail.next
            length += 1
        k %= length
        if k == 0:
            return head
        tail.next = head
        steps = length - k
        for _ in range(steps):
            tail = tail.next
        new_head = tail.next
        tail.next = None
        return new_head
```

variables: N: number of nodes in list (0 <= N <= 500)
complexity.notes: Circular link creation followed by a single split cut at offset length - (k % length).

```python
from typing import List

class Solution:
    def matrixScore(self, grid: List[List[int]]) -> int:
        m, n = len(grid), len(grid[0])
        ans = m * (1 << (n - 1))
        for j in range(1, n):
            same_as_row0 = sum(grid[i][j] == grid[i][0] for i in range(m))
            count1 = max(same_as_row0, m - same_as_row0)
            ans += count1 * (1 << (n - 1 - j))
        return ans
```

```python
# """
# This is ArrayReader's API interface.
# You should not implement it, or speculate about its implementation
# """
#class ArrayReader:
#    def get(self, index: int) -> int:

class Solution:
    def search(self, reader: 'ArrayReader', target: int) -> int:
        low, high = 0, 1
        while reader.get(high) < target:
            low = high
            high *= 2
        while low <= high:
            mid = (low + high) // 2
            val = reader.get(mid)
            if val == target:
                return mid
            elif val < target:
                low = mid + 1
            else:
                high = mid - 1
        return -1
```

```python
class Solution:
    def maxProfit(self, inventory: list[int], orders: int) -> int:
        MOD = 10**9 + 7
        lo, hi = 0, max(inventory)
        threshold = 0
        while lo <= hi:
            mid = (lo + hi) // 2
            total_sold = sum(max(0, x - mid) for x in inventory)
            if total_sold <= orders:
                threshold = mid
                hi = mid - 1
            else:
                lo = mid + 1
        profit = 0
        sold = 0
        for x in inventory:
            if x > threshold:
                cnt = x - threshold
                profit = (profit + (threshold + 1 + x) * cnt // 2) % MOD
                sold += cnt
        rem = orders - sold
        profit = (profit + rem * threshold) % MOD
        return profit
```

hints.title: Interval Sorting Strategy
hints.text: Sort intervals primarily ascending by end point, and secondarily descending by start point.

hints.title: Greedy Rightmost Placements
hints.text: Placing numbers as far to the right as possible within an interval maximizes their ability to intersect future intervals.

hints.title: Track Two Largest Chosen Elements
hints.text: Maintain the two largest elements chosen so far, say p1 and p2 with p1 < p2. If the current interval contains neither, add end minus 1 and end. If it contains only p2, add end. Update p1 and p2 accordingly.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
from typing import List

class Solution:
    def intersectionSizeTwo(self, intervals: List[List[int]]) -> int:
        intervals.sort(key=lambda x: (x[1], -x[0]))
        p1, p2 = -1, -1
        ans = 0

        for s, e in intervals:
            if s > p2:
                p1 = e - 1
                p2 = e
                ans += 2
            elif s > p1:
                p1 = p2
                p2 = e
                ans += 1

        return ans
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Set cover formulation without interval ordering is NP-hard in general graphs.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sorting intervals enables greedy selection in O(1) auxiliary memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Sort secondary start descending so shorter intervals ending at the same point are processed first.

hints.title: Longest Palindromic Prefix Focus
hints.text: Adding characters in front to create a palindrome is equivalent to finding the longest prefix of s that is already a palindrome.

hints.title: Delimiter Converted String Invariant
hints.text: In the compound string s + "#" + rev(s), the longest prefix that matches a suffix corresponds precisely to the longest palindromic prefix of s.

hints.title: Prefix LPS Calculation Procedure
hints.text: Form combined string t = s + "#" + s[::-1]. Build the prefix array lps for t. The value lps[-1] yields the length k of the longest palindromic prefix in s. Prepend the reversed remaining suffix s[k:][::-1] to original string s.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def shortestPalindrome(self, s: str) -> str:
        rev = s[::-1]
        combo = s + '#' + rev
        n = len(combo)
        lps = [0] * n
        prev = 0
        i = 1
        while i < n:
            if combo[i] == combo[prev]:
                prev += 1
                lps[i] = prev
                i += 1
            elif prev > 0:
                prev = lps[prev - 1]
            else:
                lps[i] = 0
                i += 1
        k = lps[-1]
        return rev[:len(s) - k] + s
```

variables: N: input length or search state bound
complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N) time and O(N) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing all prefixes for palindrome symmetry naively takes O(N^2) time, hitting limits on 50,000-character inputs.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: KMP prefix array evaluation on the combined string runs in O(N) time with O(N) memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should convert the longest palindromic prefix problem into a KMP string matching problem via string reversal.

```python
            idx = round(val / 17)
```

```python
import heapq

class Solution:
    def getOrder(self, tasks: list[list[int]]) -> list[int]:
        indexed = sorted([(t[0], t[1], i) for i, t in enumerate(tasks)])
        pq = []
        ans = []
        curr_time = 0
        idx = 0
        n = len(tasks)

        while idx < n or pq:
            if not pq and curr_time < indexed[idx][0]:
                curr_time = indexed[idx][0]

            while idx < n and indexed[idx][0] <= curr_time:
                heapq.heappush(pq, (indexed[idx][1], indexed[idx][2]))
                idx += 1

            duration, orig_idx = heapq.heappop(pq)
            curr_time += duration
            ans.append(orig_idx)

        return ans
```

```python
from collections import deque
from typing import List

class Solution:
    def slidingPuzzle(self, board: List[List[int]]) -> int:
        start = "".join(str(val) for row in board for val in row)
        target = "123450"
        moves = {
            0: [1, 3],
            1: [0, 2, 4],
            2: [1, 5],
            3: [0, 4],
            4: [1, 3, 5],
            5: [2, 4]
        }
        queue = deque([(start, 0)])
        visited = {start}

        while queue:
            state, step = queue.popleft()
            if state == target:
                return step
            zero_idx = state.index('0')
            state_list = list(state)
            for nxt in moves[zero_idx]:
                state_list[zero_idx], state_list[nxt] = state_list[nxt], state_list[zero_idx]
                nxt_state = "".join(state_list)
                if nxt_state not in visited:
                    visited.add(nxt_state)
                    queue.append((nxt_state, step + 1))
                state_list[zero_idx], state_list[nxt] = state_list[nxt], state_list[zero_idx]

        return -1
```

```python
class Solution:
    def medianSlidingWindow(self, nums: List[int], k: int) -> List[float]:
        window = sorted(nums[:k])
        res = []
        is_odd = (k % 2 == 1)
        mid = k // 2

        def get_median():
            if is_odd:
                return float(window[mid])
            return (window[mid - 1] + window[mid]) / 2.0

        res.append(get_median())
        for i in range(k, len(nums)):
            leaving = nums[i - k]
            entering = nums[i]
            idx = bisect.bisect_left(window, leaving)
            window.pop(idx)
            bisect.insort(window, entering)
            res.append(get_median())

        return res
```

```python
import heapq
from typing import List

class Solution:
    def smallestRange(self, nums: List[List[int]]) -> List[int]:
        heap = []
        curr_max = float("-inf")
        for i in range(len(nums)):
            heapq.heappush(heap, (nums[i][0], i, 0))
            curr_max = max(curr_max, nums[i][0])

        best_range = [float("-inf"), float("inf")]

        while heap:
            val, r, c = heapq.heappop(heap)
            if curr_max - val < best_range[1] - best_range[0]:
                best_range = [val, curr_max]
            if c + 1 == len(nums[r]):
                break
            nxt_val = nums[r][c + 1]
            curr_max = max(curr_max, nxt_val)
            heapq.heappush(heap, (nxt_val, r, c + 1))

        return best_range
```

```python
class Solution:
    def bestRotation(self, nums: list[int]) -> int:
        n = len(nums)
        diff = [0] * n
        for i, val in enumerate(nums):
            low = (i + 1) % n
            high = (i - val + n + 1) % n
            diff[low] += 1
            diff[high] -= 1
            if low >= high:
                diff[0] += 1
        best_k = 0
        max_score = -1
        curr = 0
        for k in range(n):
            curr += diff[k]
            if curr > max_score:
                max_score = curr
                best_k = k
        return best_k
```

```python
from typing import List

class Solution:
    def sortArray(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[int]:
        if len(nums) <= 1:
            return nums
        mid = len(nums) // 2
        left = self.sortArray(nums[:mid])
        right = self.sortArray(nums[mid:])
        merged = []
        i = j = 0
        while i < len(left) and j < len(right):
            if left[i] <= right[j]:
                merged.append(left[i])
                i += 1
            else:
                merged.append(right[j])
                j += 1
        merged.extend(left[i:])
        merged.extend(right[j:])
        return merged
```

```python
class Solution:
    def sortList(self, head: Optional[ListNode]) -> Optional[ListNode]:
        if not head or not head.next:
            return head
        prev = None
        slow = head
        fast = head
        while fast and fast.next:
            prev = slow
            slow = slow.next
            fast = fast.next.next
        prev.next = None
        l1 = self.sortList(head)
        l2 = self.sortList(slow)
        dummy = ListNode(0)
        curr = dummy
        while l1 and l2:
            if l1.val <= l2.val:
                curr.next = l1
                l1 = l1.next
            else:
                curr.next = l2
                l2 = l2.next
            curr = curr.next
        curr.next = l1 if l1 else l2
        return dummy.next
```

```python
class Solution:
    def generateMatrix(self, n: int) -> List[List[int]]:
        matrix = [[0] * n for _ in range(n)]
        top, bottom = 0, n - 1
        left, right = 0, n - 1
        num = 1
        while top <= bottom and left <= right:
            for c in range(left, right + 1):
                matrix[top][c] = num
                num += 1
            top += 1
            for r in range(top, bottom + 1):
                matrix[r][right] = num
                num += 1
            right -= 1
            for c in range(right, left - 1, -1):
                matrix[bottom][c] = num
                num += 1
            bottom -= 1
            for r in range(bottom, top - 1, -1):
                matrix[r][left] = num
                num += 1
            left += 1
        return matrix
```

```python
from typing import List

class Solution:
    def spiralMatrixIII(self, rows: int, cols: int, rStart: int, cStart: int) -> List[List[int]]:
        ans = [[rStart, cStart]]
        dirs = [(0, 1), (1, 0), (0, -1), (-1, 0)]
        d = 0
        step = 1
        r, c = rStart, cStart

        while len(ans) < rows * cols:
            for _ in range(2):
                dr, dc = dirs[d]
                for _ in range(step):
                    r += dr
                    c += dc
                    if 0 <= r < rows and 0 <= c < cols:
                        ans.append([r, c])
                d = (d + 1) % 4
            step += 1
        return ans
```

```python
class Solution:
    def splitListToParts(self, head: Optional[ListNode], k: int) -> list[Optional[ListNode]]:
        length = 0
        curr = head
        while curr:
            length += 1
            curr = curr.next
        base_size = length // k
        extra = length % k
        res = []
        curr = head
        for i in range(k):
            part_head = curr
            part_len = base_size + (1 if i < extra else 0)
            for _ in range(part_len - 1):
                if curr:
                    curr = curr.next
            if curr:
                nxt = curr.next
                curr.next = None
                curr = nxt
            res.append(part_head)
        return res
```

variables: N: number of nodes in list (0 <= N <= 1000)
complexity.notes: Two passes: one to count length and one to decouple k segments.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Slicing without tracking the remainder produces segments with size differences greater than 1.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Decoupling node pointers directly avoids creating new node instances beyond the output pointer array.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Handling k > N gracefully by padding remaining slots in the result with null.

hints.title: Squaring Monotonic Extremum Obstacle
hints.text: Squaring each number disrupts sorted order because negative numbers yield large positive squares. Sorting after squaring takes logarithmic factor overhead. Given that the largest squares must originate at either the far left or far right, how can you build the result in linear time?

hints.title: Extremum Inward Convergence

hints.title: Backward Fill Procedure
hints.text: Allocate an output array of length n. Set left to zero, right to n minus one, and write pointer pos to n minus one. Compute squares of values at left and right. Put the larger square at res[pos], advance the chosen boundary pointer, and decrement pos until all positions are filled.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

```python
class Solution:
    def sortedSquares(self, nums: list[int]) -> list[int]:
        n = len(nums)
        res = [0] * n
        left, right = 0, n - 1
        pos = n - 1
        while left <= right:
            left_sq = nums[left] * nums[left]
            right_sq = nums[right] * nums[right]
            if left_sq > right_sq:
                res[pos] = left_sq
                left += 1
            else:
                res[pos] = right_sq
                right -= 1
            pos -= 1
        return res
```

variables: N: length of nums array (1 <= N <= 10^4)

complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Filling from highest to lowest square achieves optimal O(N) time without extra passes.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Explaining why the maximum square is always at one of the two ends (parabolic property of x^2 centered at 0).

class Solution:
```python
    def sampleStats(self, count: list[int]) -> list[float]:
        total = sum(count)
        min_val = -1.0
        max_val = -1.0
        sum_val = 0
        mode_val = 0.0
        max_freq = 0
        
        for i, c in enumerate(count):
            if c > 0:
                if min_val == -1.0:
                    min_val = float(i)
                max_val = float(i)
                sum_val += i * c
                if c > max_freq:
                    max_freq = c
                    mode_val = float(i)
        
        mean_val = sum_val / total
        target1 = (total + 1) // 2
        target2 = (total + 2) // 2
        med1, med2 = None, None
        cur = 0

            cur += c
            if med1 is None and cur >= target1:
                med1 = i
            if med2 is None and cur >= target2:
                med2 = i
                break
        median_val = (med1 + med2) / 2.0
        return [min_val, max_val, mean_val, median_val, mode_val]
```

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from typing import Optional

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right

class Solution:
    def getDirections(self, root: Optional[TreeNode], startValue: int, destValue: int) -> str:
        def find_path(node: Optional[TreeNode], target: int, path: list[str]) -> bool:
            if not node:
                return False
            if node.val == target:
                return True
            path.append('L')
            if find_path(node.left, target, path):
                return True
            path.pop()

            path.append('R')
            if find_path(node.right, target, path):
                return True
            path.pop()

            return False

        start_path: list[str] = []
        dest_path: list[str] = []

        find_path(root, startValue, start_path)
        find_path(root, destValue, dest_path)

        i = 0
        min_len = min(len(start_path), len(dest_path))
        while i < min_len and start_path[i] == dest_path[i]:
            i += 1

        up_steps = 'U' * (len(start_path) - i)
        down_steps = ''.join(dest_path[i:])

        return up_steps + down_steps
```

hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def myAtoi(self, s: str) -> int:
        s = s.strip()
        if not s:
            return 0
        sign = 1
        i = 0
        if s[0] == '-':
            sign = -1
            i = 1
        elif s[0] == '+':
            i = 1
        res = 0
        INT_MAX = 2147483647
        INT_MIN = -2147483648
        while i < len(s) and s[i].isdigit():
            digit = ord(s[i]) - 48
            if res > (INT_MAX - digit) // 10:
                return INT_MAX if sign == 1 else INT_MIN
            res = res * 10 + digit
            i += 1
        return sign * res
```

```python
from collections import defaultdict

class Solution:
```

```python
class Solution:
    def subsets(self, nums: list[int]) -> list[list[int]]:
        res = []
        path = []
        def backtrack(start):
            res.append(list(path))
            for i in range(start, len(nums)):
                path.append(nums[i])
                backtrack(i + 1)
                path.pop()
        backtrack(0)
        return res
```
